clinician.trajectory_summary: An obese 62-year-old female with a history of cancer and chemotherapy presented with retrosternal chest pain, suspected acute coronary event. Initial ECG showed inverted T waves in anterior and lateral leads, and cardiac markers (troponin I hs, BNP, NT-proBNP) were markedly elevated. Coronary angiography revealed only minor atherosclerotic changes, ruling out obstructive coronary artery disease. Left ventriculography demonstrated akinesis of the apex and apical/mid-segment of the anterior wall with an ejection fraction of 38%. During hospitalization, an echocardiographic examination showed improved left ventricular contractive function with an ejection fraction of 47%, which confirmed the diagnosis of TTS. The patient's hospitalization was devoid of complications, and retrosternal pain did not reoccur. She was discharged on the 4th day with medications including acetylsalicylic acid, bisoprolol, ramipril, atorvastatin, pantoprazole, iron, and thyroid hormones, and referred for further surgical and oncological treatment.
